Methods for tidymodels objects

Source: R/tidymodels.R
tidymodels-methods.Rd

Fitted parsnip model objects (model_fit) and fitted workflows objects (workflow) are unwrapped with hardhat::extract_fit_engine() and the generic is then called on the underlying engine model. All other arguments, such as tree, add_statistics, or data, are passed to the method for the engine model; see the documentation for that model's method.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'model_fit'
extract_rules(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'workflow'
extract_rules(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'model_fit'
active_predictors(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'workflow'
active_predictors(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'model_fit'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'workflow'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'model_fit'
as.party(obj, ...)

# S3 method for class 'workflow'
as.party(obj, ...)

# S3 method for class 'model_fit'
var_imp(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'workflow'
var_imp(object, ...)

Arguments

x, obj, object

A fitted model_fit or workflow object.

...

Other arguments passed to the method for the engine model.

Value

The result of the generic applied to the engine model.

Details

For as.party(), engines that need the training data (e.g., xgboost) require it via data. For workflows, this should be the preprocessed predictors that were given to the engine.

Examples

if (rlang::is_installed(c("parsnip", "ranger"))) {
  library(parsnip)

  rf_fit <-
    rand_forest(trees = 5) |>
    set_engine("ranger") |>
    set_mode("regression") |>
    fit(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)

  num_ensemble_members(rf_fit)
  extract_rules(rf_fit, tree = 1:2, data = mtcars)
}
